gcm_term.reading_rule: What the curved light adds to a flat column of the same air (curved_light_w_m2): the sphere's light on the flat column's own layers, less the pseudo-spherical column's, per square metre of ground per unit of sunlight at the beam, by the solar elevation at the ground point, to the ground and to each GCM layer (top first). Nothing outside the elevations given. Added to the GCM's own shortwave it keeps PlaSim's calibrated column and supplies the twilight, the low Sun's side light and the curved scattered light. The cone (cone_w_m2), the more sunlight the widening shells above each square metre take, is left out: those shells emit their infrared from the same wider area, which a flat model's longwave leaves out too. The terms are clear sky: a model with cloud adds each layer's in the clear share above that layer and the ground's in the whole column's (the GCM runner's NTWLCLEAR).

gcm_term_cone.reading_rule: The cone the GCM term leaves out, by GCM layer (top first) and solar elevation, as in gcm_term.

longwave.reading_rule: The infrared leaving the top of the design column (clear sky, its temperatures), W/m2 per square metre of ground: through flat layers, and through the same layers as spherical shells, which take in more sunlight (the cone and the curved light) and lose more infrared by the same geometry: the shells' widening (cone) and the escape below the horizontal past the Moon's limb (curved). By GCM layer (top first) and by shell (bottom-up) each with its design temperature, so a model may scale them with its own; the ground's share apart. Clear sky: a model with cloud lets each layer's escape through the clouds above it.

evidence: The ledger's own terms by shell (six significant figures) shared among the level set's layers by their overlap in sigma, as the ledger shares them among PlaSim's ten; a regridding of the calculation the ledger records, not a new one.
reading_rule: gcm_term, gcm_term_cone and longwave read as in the ledger, on the level set's layers (top first) in place of PlaSim's ten. check: the same arithmetic on the ten levels against the ledger's own terms (largest absolute difference, per unit sunlight at the beam or W/m2, beside the largest term), and on the set the sums over the layers the grids do not share against the ledger's over the same range, and the shared layers against the ledger's.
